content:
This blog explains the Dwarka Expressway route map with sectors and interchanges in plain language. No technical jargon. No brochure-style promises. Just how connectivity works on the ground.

What Is Dwarka Expressway?

Dwarka Expressway, officially called the Northern Peripheral Road (NPR), is a high-capacity road created to directly connect:

  • Dwarka, Delhi
  • New Gurgaon
  • NH-48 (Delhi–Jaipur Highway)

It was planned as an alternative to NH-48, which had become overloaded years ago. Anyone travelling between West Delhi, South-West Delhi, and Gurgaon knows how unpredictable that highway can be.

Dwarka Expressway Route Map: The Big Picture

If you look at the route map, the expressway forms a clean diagonal link between Delhi and Gurgaon.

In simple terms, this is how it runs:

  • Starts near Dwarka Sector 21 on the Delhi side
  • Runs almost parallel to NH-48
  • Passes through several New Gurgaon sectors
  • Ends near Kherki Daula / Manesar, where it reconnects with NH-48

The total length is around 29 kilometres, with roughly:

  • 18 km in Gurgaon
  • 11 km in Delhi

title: What Is RERA and Why It Matters So Much When Buying Property in India
excerpt: What is RERA approval, really? Why was RERA introduced in the first place? And more importantly, what actually happens if a builder delays possession under RERA? Understanding RERA isn't optional. It's essential.
content:
What is RERA approval, really?
Why was RERA introduced in the first place?
And more importantly, what actually happens if a builder delays possession under RERA?

These aren't abstract legal questions. Instead, they're deeply personal ones. Because when you buy property, you're not just signing papers — you're committing savings, loans, and years of planning.

Therefore, understanding RERA isn't optional. It's essential.

And that's exactly why RERA matters.

So, What Is RERA?

Simply put, RERA stands for Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016.

In other words, it is a law created to protect homebuyers and bring transparency into the real estate sector.

More specifically, each state has its own RERA authority. As a result, builders must register their projects before selling units. In addition, buyers can check project details publicly through official portals.

Before RERA: What Property Buying Used to Feel Like

To understand why RERA is important, we first need to look backward.

Before RERA came into effect in 2016, property buying in India was often uncertain. In fact, many buyers booked apartments based largely on brochures and verbal promises. However, delivery timelines frequently extended beyond the committed dates.

Why 2026 Is an Interesting Time for First Time Home Buyers?

If you've been watching the market closely, you'll notice something: housing demand isn't slowing down — it's evolving.

More young professionals are buying earlier. Dual-income couples are entering the market faster. Rental prices in metro cities have climbed sharply. And frankly, paying ₹35,000–₹50,000 monthly rent makes you rethink your life choices.

That's where ownership starts to make sense.

However, before jumping in, let's break down the exact roadmap for First Time Home Buyers

This blog covers everything — from steps to buying a house for the first time, understanding home loans for first time buyers, and practical tips for first time home buyer success — in a real, human way. No jargon. No unrealistic promises. Just clarity.

Step 1: Get Financially Honest (Before You Even Visit a Property)

This is where most first time home buyers make mistakes.

They visit properties first.
They fall in love.
Then they check eligibility.

Reverse that.

Ask Yourself:

  • How stable is your income?
  • How much do you have saved for down payment?
  • Do you have emergency funds left after paying booking amount?
  • Are there other EMIs already running?

A healthy rule:
Your total EMIs (including home loan) should not exceed 40–45% of your monthly income.
